title: European Parenting Leave Policies
text:
We looked at how parenting leave policies change throughout time across different European countries. The data are taken from TidyTuesday 6-02-2026.

library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(gganimate)
library(magick)
library(broom)


eplp <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2026/2026-06-02/eplp.csv')


europe <- ne_countries(continent = "europe", returnclass = "sf")
yrs <- sort(unique(eplp$year))

p <- europe |>
    mutate(country2 = ifelse(iso_a2_eh == "GB", "UK", iso_a2_eh)) |>
    tidyr::expand_grid(year = yrs) |>
    st_as_sf() |>
    left_join(eplp, by = c("country2" = "country", "year")) |>
    ggplot() +
    geom_sf(aes(fill = jp_ld_m)) +
    coord_sf(xlim = c(-10, 45), ylim = c(27,84)) +
    theme_minimal() +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "#ff0099") +
    transition_states(year, transition_length = 0, state_length = 1) +
        labs(title = "year: {closest_state}")

    animate(p)

eplp |>
    ggplot(aes(x = par1_ld, y = jp_ld_m, color = year)) +
    geom_point() +

    facet_wrap( ~ par2_for_whom) +
    theme_minimal() +
    scale_color_gradient(low = "white", high = "#ff0099")

title: UK Baby Names
text:
We looked at baby name popularity in the UK over time. Since the dataset had many names I specifically tried to pick unisex names to see the difference between female and male name popularity. The data are taken from TidyTuesday 6-16-2026.

library(tidyverse)


england_wales_names <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2026/2026-06-16/england_wales_names.csv')
ni_names <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2026/2026-06-16/ni_names.csv')
scotland_names <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2026/2026-06-16/scotland_names.csv')


scotland_names |>
filter(Name %in% c("Taylor", "Sam", "Charlie", "Alex", "Blake")) |>
ggplot(aes(x = Year, y = Number, shape = Sex)) +
geom_point(color = "purple") +
geom_line(aes(color=Name)) +
labs(title = "baby names")

title: Love Island USA
Commodity Prices
Foundation Shades
text:
We looked at the shades of four foundations: Armani Luminos Silk Foundation, Charlotte Tilbury Flawless Filter Foundation, Fenty Pro Filter Foundation, and Haus Labs Triclone Skin Tech Foundation. The HEX color of each shade was taken from screenshots of the make-up provided by Sephora.
Armani Luminos Silk has a good number of options but a small range of shades, with few that are particularly light or dark. Charlot tillburry Flawless Filter Foundation has very few shades and none that are particularly dark. Fenty Pro Filter Foundation has the second-most shades but the widest range of light and dark shades. Haus Labs has the most shades, including many darker shades but doesn’t get as light as Fenty.

library(tidyverse)


# Haus Labs
df_HL <- data.frame(
    hex = c("#3F1E0B", "#4B2511", "#6A3E32", "#6D3D33", "#8A5B2D", "#6F3A0E", "#6D3C22", "#7B4D3D", "#6E3D33", "#5A352F", "#5C2E2E", "#8E5D1F", "#7E4C2F", "#9E622E", "#B36F43", "#A36A5A", "#A66D4B", "#B67E5F", "#7F4A2B", "#B57B5B", "#B68D71", "#B98B6E", "#C69A7E", "#CDA28B", "#C79A7A", "#C49B7C", "#C8A88D", "#C9A18D", "#D1B29B", "#D7B8A5", "#D7BCA8", "#E4C3B0", "#DDB9A8", "#D6B3A4", "#DCC0B2", "#D2B3A7", "#D6BBAE", "#D7BBAE", "#E3C1B3", "#E7C7B6", "#E7C4B2", "#EBC7B0", "#E7C7B0", "#EBC7B0", "#F4D1BC", "#F3D6C1", "#F0D2B7", "#F0D2B7", "#F6D8BC", "#F6D9C0", "#F6D8BC", "#F6D8BC", "#F6D8BC", "#F2E6E3"), 
    brand = "Haus Labs",
    product = "Triclone Skin Tech") 


# Charlotte Tilbury
df_CT <- data.frame(
    hex = c("#F0DCCB", "#E8CDBB", "#D3A773", "#E7BFA9", "#DCC6AB", "#D5A37F", "#E5BDA5", "#D7B27A", "#E0B69C", "#B47C52", "#D3A58E", "#A8795C"),
    brand = "Charlotte Tilbury",
    product = "Flawless Filter")

# Armani
df_A <- data.frame(
    hex = c("#E6B98E", "#E3B68F", "#E0B57F", "#DDAA72", "#E5B58E", "#E0B17C", "#DDB38A", "#D5A77C", "#D8A879", "#D7A97E", "#D2A278", "#C99A6D", "#D19C6B", "#D0A17D", "#C89A67", "#CD9C74", "#C69A6E", "#C98551", "#C99367", "#C79365", "#BD8B61", "#C78B60", "#B98253", "#B67846", "#C38B65", "#A9784E", "#B47C54", "#B57B4B", "#C58C69", "#AA794E", "#9F6B3F", "#A66E45", "#A8734C", "#9E693F", "#8F5A32", "#925F3E", "#9A623C", "#8C4C29", "#8D5C3E", "#885B3F", "#875A3E", "#805137", "#673B29", "#6B4030"),
    brand = "Armani",
    product = "Luminous Silk")

# Fenty
df_F <- data.frame(
    hex = c("#492E1D", "#502C1C", "#58361F", "#552F20", "#653F28", "#663F27", "#7C5437", "#81512E", "#96603D", "#835332", "#99623E", "#A46F45", "#976239", "#9E6231", "#A46E43", "#C08660", "#B98353", "#AD7D52", "#B88450", "#B68558", "#CA9561", "#C99564", "#CA9464", "#C3966C", "#D1A77A", "#D8B385", "#DEB38D", "#CEAA81", "#D7AB85", "#DCB286", "#D3AA86", "#D3A671", "#D8B092", "#E0BB92", "#E5BC99", "#D9B08A", "#E1BE9F", "#EAC69E", "#E9C59D", "#D6B591", "#E4C1A8", "#F0D0AE", "#EAD5BD", "#EDD5BA", "#E7CA96", "#EDD5BA", "#DCBC9B", "#F9E3D1", "#F9E7DC", "#F9E7DE"),
    brand = "Fenty Beauty",
    product = "Pro Filter")

makeup <- rbind(df_HL, df_CT, df_A, df_F)


df_plot <- makeup |>
  group_by(brand) |>
  mutate(
    id = row_number(),
    x = (id - 1) %% 10,
    y = (id - 1) %/% 10,
    hex = sort(hex),
    brand_prod = paste(brand, product, sep = "\n")
  ) |>
  ungroup()

ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = x, y = -y)) +
  geom_tile(
    aes(fill = hex),
    width = 0.95,
    height = 0.95
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ brand_prod) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  coord_equal() +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(
      size = 12,
    ),
    panel.spacing = unit(2, "lines")
  )
